subject: Clarify: how prefix/prefetch cache hits are billed (rate card & trial allocation)
body:
Message 1 (original)
From: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cloudfolio.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudfolio.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Question on prefix cache billing and trial allocation

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look great. Before we move into procurement we need to clarify how Redwood bills for cached responses. A few specific questions from our SRE and finance teams:

- If CloudFolio warms a result set via prefetch (server-side warm-up), does the cached hit count as billable compute or is it treated as a zero-cost cache hit?
- If an incoming request matches a prefix-cache entry exactly (same prompt tokens, same model+version), are generation tokens billed to us?
- Are cache fills (the act of storing a response during normal traffic) charged differently from cache reads?
- For the free trial/POC credits you offered, how should we expect those credits to apply to cache-heavy workloads?

We attached a small spreadsheet with some sample traffic slices (prefetch vs user-driven) — can you annotate how those map to billing lines? Also, if you have a short one-pager that describes eligible cache-hit criteria, that would be helpful for procurement.

Appreciate a crisp breakdown we can share with finance/security.

Best,
Sam
Procurement, CloudFolio

---

Message 2 (reply)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cloudfolio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, procurement@cloudfolio.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on prefix cache billing and trial allocation

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details below so you can share with finance/security.

TL;DR
- Cache reads that fully satisfy a request (no model compute) are not charged for generation tokens.
- Cache fills (when a request causes the model to generate and the result is stored) are billed as normal generation compute. Prefetches that execute the model (i.e., warm with actual generation) are billed.
- Eligibility requires same model+version, same prompt template (after normalization), and that the prefix/kv window still matches; partial-KV matches that require additional tokens are billed for the incremental generation.
- Trial/POC credits apply first to billed generation (cache-fill) activity; cache-hit reads that are free still reduce total billable compute but do not consume credits.

Detailed mapping (please forward to your finance team):
1) Cache read vs fill
   - Read: If the cached response is returned without invoking the model runtime (a true cache hit), we do not bill generation tokens. Read throughput is still subject to request-level rate limits, but not per-token generation charges.
   - Fill: Any request that causes the runtime to execute (first time or evicted entry re-populated) is billed the usual token-generation price. That includes prefetch runs that actually call the model.

2) Prefetch behavior
   - Prefetch that issues a real generation call = billed (counted as a fill).
   - Prefetch using a lightweight verification call (metadata-only or HEAD-style probe) does not create a generation that produces cacheable content unless explicitly configured; in that case it is not billed as generation.

3) Exact vs partial matches
   - Exact match (same normalized prompt + model+version + same system instructions) => served from cache => not billed.
   - Partial prefix match (cached prefix + request extends beyond cached content) => billed for additional tokens generated for the suffix; the cache contributes zero-cost tokens for the prefix if it avoids compute, but we only discount tokens that the runtime did not generate.

4) Trial and credits
   - POC credits are applied to billed generation and not to cache-read operations. So if your workload is heavily cache-hit dominated, your credits will mostly be consumed by the smaller set of cache-fill events (or policy-driven prefetch fills). This effectively increases the fraction of free-serving you get during POC, but credits will not be shown as consumed by cache reads.

5) Practical examples (based on your spreadsheet)
   - Row A (user-driven repeat queries): 85% cache-hit rate => 85% of those requests will not incur generation charges; the 15% that miss will be billed and consume credits.
   - Row B (prefetch warm every hour with a full generation): each warm action is billed as a fill. If you warm 1000 keys/hour, you will see generation volume for those 1000 warm events.

Attachments: I added our short ratecard excerpt and a one-page cache-eligibility checklist (PDF) to this thread. Karthik will follow up with the formal quote and a suggested trial allocation formula that maps POC usage to the initial commit.

Let me know if you want this boiled down to a one-slide doc for the CFO.

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Message 3 (internal follow-up)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cloudfolio.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on prefix cache billing and trial allocation

Adding a couple of rate-card specifics from the standard hosted API SKU so finance can model this. Short bullets below — I'll attach a sample proforma to the HubSpot deal.

- Base generation price (hosted, standard model family): $0.008 / 1k gen tokens (example SKU in excerpt).
- Cache-fill (generation) is billed at the same gen rate.
- Cache-read (true hit) = $0 / gen-tokens (no generation charge).
- We bill a small per-request serving fee for very high qps on cache reads only if you exceed edge L7 throughput thresholds (this is separate from token charges and only applies in rare, enterprise scale cases; will not affect typical POC).
- For trials: we recommend reserving 30% of POC credits to cover expected prefetch fills (so you don't accidentally warm everything and burn the credit quickly). Example formula: estimated_unique_warms * avg_gen_tokens_per_warm * gen_price = warm_budget.

I'll upload the proforma and an example warm-budget worksheet to the HubSpot deal by EOD.

Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cloudfolio.com>

Subject: Re: Question on prefix cache billing and trial allocation

Tessa / Karthik — this is exactly what procurement needed, thanks. Two quick clarifications so we can close the PO:
1) For the per-request serving fee you mentioned — can you confirm the qps threshold and an approximate unit price? (we're currently estimating peak 12k rps on reads)
2) Can you confirm whether prefetch fills triggered by a serverless cron in our VPC Private deployment would be billed the same as hosted-prefetch fills? (we need to know to size budgets for Private vs Hosted).

If you can drop those two details I'll push the PO through. Also confirm that the attached example-request-log-snippet is enough for your team to validate our traffic breakdown.

Best,
Sam
